item.title: Does Sharia law have an influence in Scotland?
item.description: Sharia law is a contentious issue in the UK. Some question whether it is compatible with so-called British values while claiming it's a separate legal system operating parallel to UK laws. In our latest De-noiser, we look at the facts.

item.title: 'Culture of fear': allegations of mismanagement keep coming at scandal hit heritage agency
item.description: New allegations at Stirling Castle dating back eight years have emerged following a string of complaints about its custodians, Historic Environment Scotland, in recent months.

item.title: No evidence of viral Richard Tice quote on Reform's plans for Scotland
item.description: A quote attributed to Reform UK's Richard Tice has gone viral in recent weeks.

item.title: ‘Weak’ salmon farm watchdog: 100 investigations and just two warning letters
item.description: Investigations into allegations of poor fish welfare at salmon farms by the UK Animal and Plant Health Agency have risen by more than ten times in six years, while site inspections have decreased.

item.title: ‘Fighting age males’ and coded swastikas: How the far-right is using gaming to recruit the next generation of Nazis
item.description: Far right actors have used gaming to recruit youngsters for some time but experts say they are increasingly using codes and imagery to avoid moderation.

item.title: Has the Scottish Government changed its stance on oil and gas?
item.description: With a decision on the Rosebank oil field imminent – and lobbying around the windfall tax at fever pitch – some are questioning whether the Scottish Government's current stance on oil and gas is in step with their ambition to be a world leader in climate action.

item.title: More than half a million tonnes of sewage sludge spread on Scotland's fields
item.description: Huge volumes of sewage sludge have been used to fertilise Scottish farmland. Studies show it contains microplastics, forever chemicals and cancer-linked pollutants.

item.title: ‘Sickening’ videos of damaged salmon at highland farm
item.description: Campaigners complained to a government animal welfare watchdog, with videos of badly injured salmon at a fish farm. This prompted a review, but should more have been done?

item.title: Revealed: Shop where Glasgow fire started had not registered to sell vapes or paid business taxes
item.description: A Ferret investigation has found there was no registration to sell vapes at the Union Street premises in Glasgow where a major fire started - and we can reveal the name of the company behind the shop.

item.title: Claim Scottish Labour built six houses in government is False
item.description: Online claims questioned Scottish Labour's house building in government between 1999 and 2007.
